title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (Grothendieck's notation in this part of the Longue Marche sequel). Let pi_{0,3} be the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,infinity}, a free profinite group on two generators. Let Gamma^+_{0,3} be the profinite Teichmüller modular group of type (0,3), extended by the outer symmetries of the three marked points. It sits in an exact sequence

 1 -> pi_{0,3} -> Gamma^+_{0,3} -> C^+_{0,3} = S_3 -> 1.

The heading 'Mise en équations dans Sl(2,Z^)' points to the classical model of this extension. The discrete group Gamma(2) is free of rank 2 and is identified with pi_1 of P^1 minus 3 points. It sits inside PSL(2,Z), which is isomorphic to Z/2 * Z/3, and PSL(2,Z)/Gamma(2) = PSL(2,F_2), which is isomorphic to S_3. So Gamma^+_{0,3} is (the profinite completion of) PSL(2,Z), i.e. the free profinite product Z/2 *^ Z/3. It has generators sigma_infty of order 2 and rho of order 3, lifting a transposition and a 3-cycle of S_3.

Problem. Parametrize automorphisms u of Gamma^+_{0,3} that induce the identity on S_3. Equivalently, these are automorphisms of pi_{0,3} compatible with the outer S_3-action; since pi is centre-free, such an automorphism extends uniquely. This is the step toward writing the defining equations of (a version of) the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group as automorphisms of this extension.

Step 1. Because u is the identity mod pi, u(sigma_infty) = h sigma_infty and u(rho) = g rho, with h, g in pi. Since sigma_infty and rho generate, u is determined by (h, g).

Step 2. The images must satisfy the defining relations (h sigma_infty)^2 = (g rho)^3 = 1. Expanding, with sigma(x) = sigma x sigma^{-1}:
- (h sigma)^2 = h sigma(h) sigma^2 = h sigma(h);
- (g rho)^3 = g rho(g) rho^2(g) rho^3 = g rho(g) rho^2(g).
Hence the conditions h sigma_infty(h) = 1 and g rho(g) rho^2(g) = 1. These are the 'two-cycle' and 'three-cycle' cocycle conditions.

Step 3. Since Gamma^+ is the free profinite product with only the relations sigma^2 = rho^3 = 1, no further relation linking g and h is needed at this stage. The pair (g, h) gives an endomorphism. One still has to check the 'condition liminaire', that u is actually an automorphism.

Step 4 (next page). The pair is re-read as commutator data: [u, rho] = int(g) and [u, sigma_infty] = int(h). Compatibility with the 'lacet' structure is then added: u(l_i) = int(g_i) l_i^p with p in Z^*, for i in {0, 1, infinity}.

In modern terms: this is the derivation of Drinfeld's relations (I) f(x,y)f(y,x) = 1 and (II) the pentagon-free 3-cycle relation, f(z,x) z^m f(y,z) y^m f(x,y) x^m = 1. They are obtained as the conditions for (f, lambda) to define an automorphism of PSL(2,Z^) = Z/2 *^ Z/3 (equivalently of B^_3 modulo its centre) restricting suitably to the free group.
errors: 'Soit u un automorph. de pi_{0,3} — ou ce qui revient au même, un automorph. de Gamma^+_{0,3} qui induit l'identité dans S_3' is imprecise. Only automorphisms of pi_{0,3} commuting with the outer S_3-action correspond to such automorphisms of Gamma^+. The correspondence is then bijective because pi_{0,3} is centre-free.

Surjectivity/bijectivity of the endomorphism defined by arbitrary (h, g) satisfying (2) is not automatic. Grothendieck flags this himself as the 'condition liminaire'; the parenthetical as written ('que (3) sont des relations génératrices') slightly conflates the presentation with the invertibility check.

ideas.what: Viewing pi_{0,3} as a normal subgroup of the extension Gamma^+_{0,3} = (PSL(2,Z))^ = Z/2 *^ Z/3 with quotient S_3, and parametrizing S_3-trivial automorphisms by a pair (h, g) in pi^2
ideas.modern_name: Gamma(2) inside PSL(2,Z); automorphisms of the profinite completion of PSL(2,Z) / B_3 modulo centre, used to define GT^
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990) for the relations; Ihara; Lochak–Schneps for the B_3 / PSL_2 viewpoint
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme only sketches the 'tour de Teichmüller' with the (0,3) and (0,4) levels; the explicit equations are not there as far as I know

ideas.what: Conditions h sigma(h) = 1 and g rho(g) rho^2(g) = 1 as the translation of the order-2 and order-3 relations
ideas.modern_name: Two-cycle (I) and three-cycle (II) relations defining GT^

ideas.what: Interpretation of (g, h) as commutators [u, rho] = int(g), [u, sigma] = int(h) (next page)
ideas.modern_name: Cocycle description of automorphisms of an extension with centre-free kernel

missed.claim: Grothendieck independently wrote, before Drinfeld (1990), the two-cycle/three-cycle equations of a GT-type group as the conditions for an automorphism of Z/2 *^ Z/3 = PSL(2,Z^) fixing S_3. This is a priority/historical detail rather than a new result; the mathematics is now standard (Drinfeld, Ihara, Lochak–Schneps).
missed.quote: h sigma_infty(h) = 1    g rho(g) rho^2(g) = 1, exprimant respectivement les relations (h sigma_infty)^2 = (g rho)^3 = 1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents the pre-Drinfeld origin of the GT^ equations in Grothendieck's own notes. Of historical interest only.

deep.surprise_reason: Correct, routine derivation of the order-2/order-3 relations that later became Drinfeld's relations (I) and (II). It is historically interesting as an independent pre-1990 formulation, but the content is fully known in the literature.
transcription_corrections: Margin likely reads 'Ces notations seront revisées encore une fois au § 46' rather than 'revisées en ? très au § 46'.
Header after 'Mise en équations dans Sl(2,Z^).' is probably '[automorphismes / commutant] extérieurs : S_3' (partly struck); uncertain.
The second occurrence 'deux élts de ... au-dessus de sigma_infty-dot et de rho-dot' may refer to C^+_{0,3} (the quotient) for the dotted elements; the lifts sigma_infty, rho are in Gamma^+_{0,3}.
'Nous' is struck and replaced by 'Pour le moment'; correctly noted.
